title.narrative: EU Sustainable Forest and Cocoa Programme

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU Sustainable Forest and Cocoa Programme - The Overall Objective of this action is To accelerate the transition of Ghana¿s agricultural sector toward sustainability, resilience, inclusivity and food security.The implementation of this action will contribute to smart, green and digital economic recovery in Ghana (TEI). The Specific Objectives of this action are to:1      Improve the sustainability and climate-resilience of agricultural production in northern Ghana2      Improve access to markets for sustainably-grown produce in northern Ghana3      Improve forest management and sustainable cocoa production in Ghana The Outputs to be delivered by this action contributing to the corresponding Specific Objectives are:-       Contributing to Specific Objective 1:1.1 Sustainable crop value chains developed1.2 Improved capacity of farmers for using sustainable practices 1.3 Improved access of smallholders to inputs and services  -       Contributing to Specific Objective 2:2.1 Improved capacity of Value Chains Associations and FBOs in supporting access to market for their members2.2 Improved capacity of district and local actors, FBOs and farmers for applying Quality Management Systems and Good Agricultural Practices, including climate-adapted, smart agricultural practices for their produce.2.3 Improved capacity of community processors to meet markets requirements in their value chains. -       Contributing to Specific Objective 3:3.1 Improved capacity of the cocoa value chain actors in working together and ensuring sustainable cocoa production in Ghana 3.2 Improved capacity of FLEGT-related multi-stakeholder platforms 3.3 Facilitated landscape restoration with the support of the Action

title.narrative: Outcome 3 Improved capacity of FLEGT multistakeholder platforms

description.narrative: Since signing the VPA in November 2009 with the EU, Ghana has been working to put in place a Timber Legality Assurance System and to undertake the necessary reforms to ensure better forest governance. In this context, the FLEGT multistakeholders platforms established to accompany the implementation of the VPA remain not only relevant but critical in maintaining momentum and ensuring resolve to address all issues to reach the objectives of the FLEGT VPA. The intervention proposed under this component will support the FLEGT multistakeholder platforms to continue their monitoring and observation roles as well as to ensure their meaningful participation in the VPA implementation process. The particular actions will be developed in detail at a later stage as appropriate and under the guidance and request Delegation of the European Union to Ghana. EFIs intervention under this component is separate from the process support to the EUGhana VPA formerly provided under the VPA ALA Facility (end of applicable contribution agreement between EFI and INTPA F2 in July 2024). The EFI intervention shall complement the support provided by the VPA implementation programme currently provided by AFD and any other forthcoming EU funded support to VPA/FLEGT licensing process and in this context, shall ensure that its activities concur with those under programmes also, under the guidance of the Delegation of the European Union to Ghana. EFI intervention will particularly focus on sub granting financial resources to local CSOs to support multistakeholder activities in the areas like VPA independent observation, forest restoration and tree tenure reforms.

title.narrative: Outcome 1 Strengthened EU Ghana cooperation on sustainable cocoa

description.narrative: The EU and Ghana launched a policy dialogue on sustainable cocoa in March 2021. While there are no interinstitutional coordination mechanisms nor policy document existing on sustainable cocoa, results of the policy dialogue with COCOBOD on the one hand, and the EU deforestation regulation on the other hand, provide some elements for framing the partnership between the EU and Ghana.This component will support the structuring and facilitation of the policy dialogue into a process that will enable inclusive and transparent participation of stakeholders. The component will provide the technical expertise and support for the EU and Ghana to build a common understanding on the definition of sustainable cocoa and progress on the implementation of the key actions of the Sustainable Cocoa Alliance Roadmap, as well as ensure the visibility of Ghanas progress towards more sustainable cocoa production and compliance with EU legislation.

title.narrative: Level of implementation of the Sustainable Cocoa Alliance Roadmap

description.narrative: This qualitative indicator is designed to assess to what extent the Sustainable Cocoa Alliance Roadmap and associated work packages are implemented.

comment.narrative: Collaboration established with implementation activities of the road map initiated only in some areas without structured and systematic dialogue.
Good to a significant degree. a. various actions of the strategy implemented at national and local level b. multistakeholder engagement is effective through a national process End 2025

title.narrative: Outcome 2 Increased transparency and sustainability monitoring of cocoa production

description.narrative: The implementation of Ghana sustainable cocoa objectives and the compliance of Ghanaian cocoa with future EU requirements strongly rely on country stakeholders ability to put in place robust and integrated tools and information systems that ensure the traceability and sustainability monitoring of cocoa. To ensure their credibility and trust by stakeholders, these tools and information systems should be based on consensual definitions, methodologies and data transparency, and embedded in coherent standards. In addition, these should be connected to risk management and mitigation responses on the ground. Subnational actors, such as regional governments, companies and civil society actors, have an important role to play to support the implementation of cocoa traceability and sustainability risk monitoring, mitigation and remediation on the ground and should be capacitated to do so.This component will provide technical assistance at national level to ensure the implementation of robust traceability and sustainability monitoring systems and processes, that respond to the needs of all supplychain actors. It will provide support to national stakeholders to discuss and align national, regional and EU standards for sustainable cocoa and test innovative approaches at subnational level to engage actors on the ground in sustainability risk monitoring and mitigation, and support cocoa producing regions, in particular highrisk areas, in their transition towards sustainability.EFIs work under this component complements the ongoing work of the Sustainable Cocoa Programme, in particular on traceability and child labour (implemented by GIZ). title.narrative: Output 4.1 related to Outcome 4: Identified best practices for restoration approaches in Ghana

description.narrative: This output will evaluate existing restoration and cocoa agroforestry approaches, lessons learned on incentives and effective implementation, and recommendations for future engagement of stakeholders and forest restoration activities. It will help to gather knowledge on existing practices, tools, approaches, challenges, opportunities and needs. It will also help to build capacity with practitioners, CSOs, and local communities on both the technical aspects of sustainable management of forest landscapes and agroforestry systems as well as on governance, including participatory planning, decisionmaking, benefit sharing, implementation and monitoring and evaluation.This output will provide technical assistance and/or grants (outsourcing and workshops) to document and disseminate best practices for restoration activities in forested areas in Ghana, including learning from other jurisdictions in West Africa. This output will issue a service contract to recruit a consultant team to conduct the study of existing restoration activities, disseminate findings through workshops, stakeholder meetings, and/or reports, and compile feedback from stakeholders. This will provide insights into restoration activities and field interventions, priority areas, and stakeholder involvement to be supported under output 4.2.

title.narrative: Output 2.1 related to Outcome 2: Improved traceability and sustainability monitoring systems and tools

description.narrative: This output will support stakeholders in defining a consensual approach to trace cocoa and monitor cocoa sustainability, in particular related to future EU requirements, that can build trust amongst partners and inform cocoa operators sustainability risk management practices and due diligence requirements. This output will seek to support the national traceability system alignment with stakeholders needs and future EU due diligence requirements, integration or connection to relevant sustainability data and information systems and interoperability with private sector traceability systems. In addition, this output will seek to work with stakeholders to increase the transparency and accountability of traceability schemes and design appropriate governance mechanisms. This output may also support the production of relevant forest and landuse data and support Ghana in the operationalization of its forest monitoring and deforestation alert system.This output will provide technical assistance to the COCOBOD and relevant institutions such as FC (including direct support via grants), as well as cocoa supply chain stakeholders to enhance their cooperation and build trust. This output may, based on the needs and complementarity with other donor funding, support data production and/or information system piloting.

title.narrative: Output 3.2 related to Outcome 3: Tree tenure policy reform

description.narrative: Under the Ghanaian legal system, ownership of the land does not necessarily translate into ownership of the naturally occurring resources it holds, creating a plurality of rights and interests, as well as conflicts. The Constitution (Art.257) vests forest reserves in the President and their management in the government (Forestry Commission). On the other hand, offreserves, rights, interests and entitlements in land and trees are generally held by the landowner. Similarly, the Ghanaian Constitution vests the rights to natural resources, including naturallyoccurring trees, in the State, irrespective of whether it is on private or public land. The revenue from the harvesting is shared between the State and the beneficiaries listed in the Constitution. The problem with this benefitsharing arrangement is that the Constitution excludes key stakeholders, such as the farmers and forestdependent communities who end up cutting down trees illegally. The introduction of Social Responsibility Agreement (SRA) under the VPA by the State has not served adequately to incentivise farmers and local communities against illegally removing trees. The complexity of tree tenure in Ghana and the inadequacy of forest policy is largely regarded as a disincentive to sustainable forest management and as a driver of illegal logging and deforestation. Efforts towards tree tenure reforms have been ongoing for a long time but are yet to yield positive results. Despite significant consultation on this issue, there is no consensus on the most appropriate tree tenure arrangements to address the deforestation issues or on the reforms needed.Developing adequate forest policies is expected to contribute significantly to Ghanas drive to halt deforestation, enhance its forest estate and promote good forest governance (including gender informed community participation in forest resources management), and equity in forest management in the framework of its forest sector initiatives. In this context, the active involvement of the CSOs, landowners, and farmers is critical. This output will support these stakeholders to identify gaps and help design options for tree tenure regimes with accompanying benefit sharing mechanisms in Ghana. Depending on the needs identified and agreed with the Delegation of the European Union to Ghana during the implementation of the intervention, the following activities will be implemented Map relevant stakeholders and organisations in the field of tree tenure. Provide technical advice to nongovernmental stakeholders towards a process for tree tenure reform. Document and share information and knowledge related to tree tenure reform.Provide technical advice in workshops and meetings and/or technical support via grants to i) build capacity of civil society organisations on tree tenure; and ii) explore opportunities for the multistakeholder platforms to support such reform process (process to be taken forward under output 3.1).
